mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong economic growth, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which is typically associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines by more than 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side activity, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6%, it signals a loose monetary policy combined with a weak labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with weak labor market
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and UNRATE > 6% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over three months signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST shows a sustained increase over three months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% quarter-over-quarter and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals a potential economic slowdown with tight monetary policy, which is typically associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: economic slowdown with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If GDPC1 QoQ < 1% and FEDFUNDS > 2% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
